newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher on cold forecasts.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher on cold forecasts.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed higher in active trade, with buying throughout the day fueled by forecasts for crop-damaging cold this weekend from Kansas to the Texas Panhandle, traders said.
Low temperatures of 18 to 20 F degrees were forecast for the region, which could damage developing hard red winter wheat, meteorologists said.
Commercial grain firm Benson Quinn bought 3.0 million bushels each of May and July, but also sold 1.0 million each of May and July. Cargill sold about 4.0 million bushels of July, traders said.
KCBT wheat closed up 9-1/4 to seven cents, with May up 9-1/4 at $4.35-1/2 per bushel and July up 9-1/4 at $4.05-1/2.
Estimated volume Thursday was 37.74 million bushels versus 27.385 million on Wednesday.
